packages.headline: Exodus: Going Hands-on With This Wild Interactive Space Opera

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
We played Exodus, and among the trappings of a beloved genre, there's a very different - occasionally very strange - new game emerging.
Exodus: Going Hands-on With This Wild Interactive Space Opera
As I help free a talking frog the size of a small car – who also happens to be an engineer – from imprisonment, I find myself thinking, “ Exodus is a lot… weirder than I expected.”
Simply the genre of this game had me excited – this is a true throwback to choice-based action-RPGs of the past; stuffed with morality systems, crunchy, synergistic abilities, mouthy companions and weighty combat. But it’s what I didn’t go in waiting to play that leaves me most intrigued – there’s a serious, galactic-scale, hard-sci storyline here, but it’s willing to go full ’70s cosmic freakout amid all that.
Exodus presents a universe with celestial powers, science-indistinguishable-from-magic locations and, yes, highly evolved, talking animals. It was around the time that one of my companions was screaming “There’s still time to negotiate!” into the face of a charging war-bear (who we’d upset by killing her human friend) that I realized, despite drawing on an established genre, quite how different Exodus is aiming to be.
At gamescom 2026, I played a mission set several hours into the game – the game’s hero, Jun sets off on a rescue mission to save a space station (manned by hyper-intelligent frogs) from an invading force, alongside two of the game’s companions. Suliman is a reserved, slightly spiky individual, and Elise is a far more happy-go-lucky mercenary who tends to her combat duties in a combat-ready exosuit.
It’s an action-heavy slice of the game, and what struck me first was the weight and optionality of combat. Jun’s primary weapon is actually many weapons in one – the Recycler can shift form into anything from a burst-fire battle rifle to a shield-annihilating energy weapon, with the common thread being that it feels good to fire. This genre isn’t particularly known for its responsive gunplay, but the opening skirmishes – a tight mix of cover shooting and flashy ability use – were enough to convince me that this was anything but an afterthought in this game.
But beyond that, Jun can also use crafted or scavenge items like hovering, drone-like grenades, as well as an array of Celestial powers that act like cooldown timer spells in combat – letting me send eruptions of energy under enemy feet from the other side of the arena, or petrify enemies for my companions to deal with.
And speaking of those companions, Elise and Suliman also gave me a taste of how your chosen team can fundamentally alter how you choose to play. While your squad will fight autonomously, each comes with abilities that can be easily accessed and unleashed mid-fight, as well as “ultimate”-like attacks that can shift the course of a battle.

Rack up Points in Arcade Hit Railbreak DX, Out Now on XBOX Series X|S & XPA
Hello and welcome to the highest-octane arcade experience of your life! I’m Julia Wolbach, and I’m stoked to tell you all about Railbreak DX , a gore-geous on-rails shooter releasing today on XBOX Series X|S & XPA today with support for XBOX Cloud Streaming. Read on for some secret developer tips to help up your zombie-blasting game.

In this unnerving adventure through Cypress Ridge in the midst of a zombie apocalypse, you’ll find a variety of helpful supplies scattered about the city and a bevy of breakable objects. This is also the only mode where you can pick up special weapons in the environment to change up your gameplay. Lydia really is an expert markswoman! As the game’s camera control is automated, you’ll need to pay close attention and keep your reflexes sharp to find powerful and hidden weapons in each level. While you’ll always have your trusty handgun, you can find a variant of that armament in Act IV in a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it moment. As you’re strolling through the park, keep your eyes peeled on the benches for the magnum, a pistol that offers heavily increased damage. There are even more classified instruments of destruction to find in Story mode: rumor is you might find a plasma-infused SMG to try on for size!
Beyond the hilarious Story mode, a whole variety of playable Survivors await, each with their own load-outs, specific firing and damage rates, and other quirks. In the original Railbreak , there were nine characters to control, but in Railbreak DX , there are now a total of 18 magnificent mortals to experiment with in the quest for the best score.

On the opposite end, playing as Rin will up your score game at the risk of a premature death. XBOX and TCL Partner to Bring XBOX App to TCL Smart TVs
Today, we’re sharing a new partnership with TCL that will bring the XBOX app to select TCL Smart TVs in the coming months.
We want to be where the world plays. That means giving players more choice in how and where they play, making the XBOX experiences easier to access. Bringing the XBOX app to select TCL Smart TVs is another step toward that. Together, we’re making XBOX gaming more accessible than ever, enabling millions of TCL TV users across more than 25 countries to enjoy XBOX titles on the Smart TVs they already own.
To get started, you will need the XBOX app on a supported Smart TV, a supported controller, and cloud playtime included with XBOX Game Pass or sold separately. Plus, if you have Game Pass, you get an instant library of cloud playable games.
With the XBOX app on supported TCL Smart TVs, players will be able to access XBOX Cloud Gaming through their Game Pass subscription to stream supported games directly from their TV. For eligible XBOX Game Pass subscribers, that means access to an instant library of games spanning blockbuster releases, beloved franchises, and indie favorites through their cloud playtime.
Whether you’re playing on a supported TCL Smart TV, console, or PC, your games, friends, achievements, and saves travel with you across the XBOX ecosystem, making it easy to pick up and play wherever you choose.
By bringing the XBOX app to select TCL Smart TVs, we’re giving players another simple way to play their games and stay connected to their gaming community.
As we continue bringing XBOX to more devices, partnerships like TCL help us give players more flexibility to play the games they love however they want.

packages.headline: 'No One Puts Double Fine Out of Business Except for Me' — Tim Schafer Explains How He Kept Double Fine Afloat After Leaving Xbox

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Tim Schafer, game designer and founder of Psychonauts developer Double Fine, gave a strong response after Xbox divested the studio as part of its massive restructuring efforts this summer.
'No One Puts Double Fine Out of Business Except for Me' — Tim Schafer Explains How He Kept Double Fine Afloat After Leaving Xbox
Speaking with Bloomberg's Jason Schreier in a September 2026 interview , Schafer admitted that he knew something was up before Xbox’s divestment was officially announced — but he wasn’t about to go down without a fight.
"You’re like, 'Wait a second, we’re not going out like this,'" Schafer explained. "Some people said, 'I’m checking out, this is one too many battles for me.’ But for the rest of us, it’s like a creative awakening."
"No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me," he continued. "Asha’s not going to shoot my dog. I’m going to shoot it. But I’m not going to shoot it, because it’s going to do great. A lot of people want to walk the dog."
Thankfully, Double Fine was able to retain its intellectual property and become fully independent, though it did have to lay off a quarter of its staff as a result of this change. That isn’t stopping it from making more games, though, as the developer recently published a Kickstarter for its next project — with the addendum that if it raises $100 million, they’ll also make Brutal Legend 2.
And yet, in spite of these challenges, Schafer says he’s been able to find a creative spark that has invigorated both himself and the remaining team at Double Fine.
"This is the good fight. Can we think of a great idea for a game that we can actually do for the right budget, that can get to this publisher who’s interested in these types of games? This kind of problem-solving is soul-enriching. Using creativity to solve problems is what gets us up in the morning. So it is hard, and it is scary and it is stressful, but it’s at least putting some fire back into the bellies of the team and me," he said.

packages.headline: 「Claude Codeが消費したトークン」で進行するクリッカーゲーム登場。AIをぶん回すほど企業が育つ、トークン無限溶かし沼

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
本作は、Claude Codeとの連携をおこなうことにより、消費されたトークンを糧に進行するクリッカーゲームとなっている。
「Claude Codeが消費したトークン」で進行するクリッカーゲーム登場。AIをぶん回すほど企業が育つ、トークン無限溶かし沼
Preferred Networksは9月4日、『 トークン x トークン x クリッカー 』を発表した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）で、9月8日に発売予定。本作は、Claude Codeとの連携をおこなうことにより、消費されたトークンを糧に進行するクリッカーゲームとなっている。弊誌ではリリースに先駆けて本作をプレイする機会を頂いたので、詳しく紹介していく。
そんなPreferred Networksが新たに放つゲームが『トークン x トークン x クリッカー』だ。本作はそのままでもゲームとして成立する一方で、コーディングエージェントとの連携をおこなうことで、稼働量がゲーム内経済へと影響する「コンパニオンモード」をオプションで有効化することが可能。本稿ではClaude Codeとの連携によるコンパニオンモードでの利用を前提に説明を進める。なお、本作はClaude Codeを提供するAnthropicとの提携によって開発されたものではないとのこと。
ゲームを開始すると、3Dオフィスが表示される。起動時に表示されたボタンからコンパニオンモードへと切り替えれば準備完了だ。そのほかには、Claude Codeとの連携にあたって特別な操作をおこなう必要はない。
パソコンでClaude Codeを立ち上げ、新しくセッションを開始すると、ゲーム内では『Omega Crafter』の相棒キャラでもあるグラミーが従業員としてオフィスに出社する。Claude Codeでタスクをこなしている間、ゲーム内でも対応するグラミーが働いてくれるのだ。筆者は今回、自分用のメモ帳アプリを作ることにしたが、少しオフィスが寂しいので、横で別のグラミーに大阪の美味しいランチを調べさせておくことにした。プロジェクトを分ければ、オフィスのレイアウトを“部署”ごとに分けることもできる。
Claude Codeで消費したトークンの量に応じて、オフィスにはゴミ（燃えカス）が散らばる。それをマウスでクリックすることでコインを獲得可能。そしてコインを用いてアップグレードを購入することで、ゴミ1個あたりの価値を高めたり、クリック範囲を向上させたり、自動でオフィスを掃除してくれるロボット掃除機を走らせたりすることができる。
なお本作では、Claude Codeがローカルに生成するログを読み取ることで、どんなタスクをこなしているかをゲーム内にも表示しているようだ。入力や許可を待っているといった、タスクの進行状況についてもゲーム内で把握することができる。ただし、こうしたログ情報は一切外部に送信されることはないとのことだ。インターネット接続やアカウント登録は不要であり、完全なローカル動作が可能であるとアピールされている。現時点ではClaude Codeのみに対応しているとのことで、ほかのAIエージェントのサポートについては今後の対応に期待したい。
Preferred Networksは、AI技術の研究開発をおこなう日本の企業である。同社はゲーム開発会社ではないものの、ほぼエンジニアのみで構成されたチームでオープンワールド自動化サバイバル『Omega Crafter（オメガクラフター）』を手がけたという異色の経歴をもち、同作は昨年5月に正式リリースを迎えている。

packages.headline: 『鬼武者 Way of the Sword』、Steam同接「4万超え」で圧倒的盛況の滑り出し。爽快剣戟で、剣豪が令和に蘇る

カプコンは9月4日、剣戟アクションゲーム『鬼武者 Way of the Sword』をリリースした。Steamでは発売後、同時接続プレイヤー数が4万4000人を超えるといった盛況を博している。
『鬼武者 Way of the Sword』、Steam同接「4万超え」で圧倒的盛況の滑り出し。爽快剣戟で、剣豪が令和に蘇る
株式会社カプコンは9月4日、剣戟アクションゲーム『 鬼武者 Way of the Sword 』を発売した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam/Epic Gamesストア/Microsoft Store）/Nintendo Switch 2/PS5/Xbox Series X|S。本作は、本稿執筆時点でSteamでの同時接続プレイヤー数が4万4000人を突破するなど注目を集めている。
『鬼武者 Way of the Sword』は、2001年より続くアクションゲーム『鬼武者』シリーズの最新作だ。舞台となるのは、瘴気によって不可思議な姿と化した江戸時代初期の京都。プレイヤーは「鬼の篭手」によって超人的な力を得た剣豪「宮本武蔵」となり、京都にはびこる異形「幻魔」を斬り伏せながら、己が戦う理由を探し求めていく。家庭用ゲーム機向けとしては、2006年の『新 鬼武者 DAWN OF DREAMS』以来、20年ぶりの完全新作となる。
『鬼武者』の世界観と融合した、江戸時代の京都の町並みも魅力の一つ。フィールドについては、探索ができる“ワイドリニア”な京都の町と、1本道のダンジョンによって構成されている。ストーリーが進むと町の冒険できる範囲が広がるほか、のっぺらぼうなど、“実在”する妖怪などをテーマにしたサブクエスト「京都奇譚」が体験できるようになる。ちなみに主人公、武蔵のフェイスモデルには数々の時代劇映画に出演した名優、三船敏郎氏が起用されている。
レビュー集積サイト Metacritic では、発売に先立ってメタスコアが公開されており、もっともレビュー数の多いPS5版は80件以上のレビューを集め、85点の高評価を獲得。これは2004年に発売された『鬼武者3』に並ぶ、シリーズ最高評価となっている。ちなみに Nintendo Switch 2版はレビュー数11件と少ないものの、今年トップクラスの90点を獲得している。
『 鬼武者 Way of the Sword 』は、PC（Steam/Epic Gamesストア/Microsoft Store）/Nintendo Switch 2/PS5/Xbox Series X|S向けに発売中だ。
『Slay the Spire 2』を遊び込んだプレイヤーに『カオスゼロナイトメア』をおすすめしたい。“運良く作れた無双デッキ”を保存できる、『スレスパ』に似てるけどちょっと違うデッキ構築ローグライク
本作の戦闘は、タイミングよく防御する「受け流し」、敵の攻撃を跳ね返す「弾き」による剣戟アクションが核となる。敵の「力動」を削りきると体勢を崩し、「崩し一閃」によって大ダメージを与えられるほか、攻撃を受ける直前のボタン入力による「一閃」も発動可能。シリーズの代名詞と言えるバッサリ感を味わえる爽快なバトルとなっている。また、鬼の篭手によって戦闘を有利にする覚醒などスキルツリーによってさまざまなアクションを習得していく。

packages.headline: 1 vs. 100 Live Was the Kind of Incredible Creative Risk I'd Like to See Xbox Get Back To

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
I so vividly remember making the time to log on and play 1 vs. 100 in the evenings the game was available, and trying to answer those trivia questions as quickly as possible. You could get on Party Chat with your friends and root for each other to make it into The Mob -- or even The One. I never got to be The One, but I did make it into The Mob once. I fared well enough that I did win an honest-to-goodness prize: 80 Microsoft Points, which was the equivalent of $1. That's a dollar more than any other game I'd ever played had given me!
1 vs. 100 Live Was the Kind of Incredible Creative Risk I'd Like to See Xbox Get Back To
We'll do it live, f*** it!
This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.
To this day, the Achievements on my Xbox gamercard that I'm most proud of are the 12 out of 12 I got in 1 vs. 100. They are, of course, impossible to attain now, and so I will always cherish them. But 1 vs. 100 was more than a licensed video game adaptation of a popular game show. For Xbox, it was an incredibly gutsy creative risk that actually worked, and I'd love to see the company get back to that kind of boldness again.
If you're not familiar with the video game version of 1 vs. 100, it was an Xbox 360 game played live with actual Xbox players at certain times of the week when the show would be "on the air." It was, quite literally, appointment gaming. The majority of players were in The Crowd, aka the audience. You'd get to play along trying to answer the quick-response trivia questions. Meanwhile, 100 randomly selected players would get to be in The Mob, who would compete for actual prizes — free Xbox Live Arcade games and/or Microsoft Points (for those too young to remember, these were virtual currency used to buy games on the Xbox Live Marketplace or on Xbox Live Arcade). Finally, there was The One, another randomly selected player who, if they could beat The Mob in the trivia challenge, could win even bigger amounts of cash (again, in the form of Microsoft Points).
I so vividly remember making the time to log on and play in the evenings the game was available, and trying to answer those trivia questions as quickly as possible. You could get on Party Chat with your friends and root for each other to make it into The Mob — or even The One. I never got to be The One, but I did make it into The Mob once. I fared well enough that I did win an honest-to-goodness prize: 80 Microsoft Points, which was the equivalent of $1. That's a dollar more than any other game I'd ever played had given me!
Sadly, 1 vs. 100 didn't last. It had a real-life host, a crew of game and infrastructure engineers that made the live events work, server costs on Xbox Live, and goodness knows what else. I understand why Microsoft killed it, but still don't like it. 1 vs. 100 represented the kind of creative risk-taking that Xbox just doesn't do anymore. I get the franchise-first focus the new regime is taking now — and I won't lie, it'll be nice to have Fallout games more than once every 15 years, as one example — but it sure would be cool to see Asha Sharma and Matt Booty take the creative swings that made Xbox beloved and successful in the Xbox 360 era in the first place.
The concept of a live interactive video game show had so much promise and potential. As 1 vs. 100 reigned for a brief time, I remember how we would openly daydreamed together in the Official Xbox Magazine office about what other game shows could be brought to life this way: The Price is Right, Press Your Luck, or even Jeopardy and/or Wheel of Fortune. None of it ever came to pass, of course, and none of it probably ever will. But 1 vs. 100 was real, it worked

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
IGN's Logan Plant shares 14 predictions for the pair of Nintendo Directs airing in the coming days.
14 Predictions for the September 2026 Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct
Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days , and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement. On Tuesday, September 8, it’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a more general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9. While we wait, it's predictions time!
Before we start, a couple of disclaimers: these are all purely my guesses based on public information and my analysis of Nintendo’s release patterns, and nothing more. Nothing here is based on any inside information. But, I will be discussing a couple of relevant leaks over the last few months, so if you have been steering clear of information like that, you may not want to read on.
Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Predictions
Zelda is my favorite series, so I’m buzzing thinking about all the possibilities we could see Tuesday morning. But I’m trying to keep things realistic in this piece and only sharing predictions that I think have a legitimate chance of happening.
This will undoubtedly be the centerpiece of the presentation. We’ve only seen a few seconds of footage of the Ocarina of Time remake , which is set to come out in 2026. So, now’s the time for the full reveal trailer and release date. I can’t wait for this one; my imagination has been running wild over this remake for the last three months, and we’re finally going to see more about the scope of this remake. Is it faithful, or more of a reimagining? What does the kingdom of Hyrule look like beyond Link’s treehouse? All that and more will likely be answered by a more conventional trailer that gives us a proper look at the remake.
I don’t know exactly what Ocarina of Time will look like, but the teaser trailer from earlier this year tells me Nintendo is very confident in this game. You don’t set the internet’s imagination on fire with a 10-second tease of Link’s treehouse if you don’t have really satisfying answers to share when you do finally pull the curtain back, and I expect the Ocarina of Time remake to be a pretty big deal.

packages.headline: 30 Open World Masterpieces You Need to Play - IGN30

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
From web-swinging superheroes and sword-swinging monster hunters to bank heists and shrine raids, these are the 30 open world masterpieces you need to play.
30 Open World Masterpieces You Need to Play - IGN30
Open-world games. Arguably, no other genre has defined modern gaming more than the expansive, experimental, and exciting places this one has taken us to. Over the past 30 years, we’ve gone from grey, empty streets begging to be torn up in a blocky muscle car to glorious, colourful fantasy lands full of adventure and opportunity. But what are the games that have stood out the most, pushed the form forward, and ultimately led to GTA 6’s moment?
As part of IGN 30, I’m going to try to answer that question by walking you through five distinct flavours of open-world game before deciding on the greatest of them all. From web-swinging superheroes and sword-swinging monster hunters to bank heists and shrine raids, here are the 30 masterpieces of open-world game design.
Claude’s violent journey through the streets of Liberty City set the template for the next 10 years of copycats — a few of which we’ll look at in a short while. It took a setting first sketched out in the original GTA and combined it with the sort of cinematic storytelling emerging on PlayStation at the time to perform alchemy. The result was a first of its kind and a new gold standard for open worlds.
They may feel like monotonous, clunky missions to play through now, but there’s no denying the permanent blueprint GTA 3 created for expansive city games to come, nor the way it managed to successfully weave a story that evoked prestige television into an open world structure — casting multiple Sopranos alumni in the process. It took the pulsating urban driving experience pioneered in Driver, a 1999 open-zone car chaser, and presented it in a wholly new way. Sure, there were open-world city games before GTA 3, but not many others on this list would exist without it.
Tommy Vercetti’s tale offered virtual time travel back to an exaggerated 1980s that felt like a love fist to the face back in 2002. GTA 3’s city served its street-level crime story perfectly, but Vice City created a sandbox you wanted to spend time in, regardless of plot momentum. Yes, its hit-filled radio stations played a huge part in creating its vibe, but so did its numerous landmarks and distinct gang-controlled regions that made this slice of fictional Florida feel alive.
It felt more like existing in a world, and gave you the opportunity to soak in its culture in a way GTA 3 never did — managing to still provide a propulsive story, but allowing more time to breathe in between missions. In this respect, it borrowed aspects from an even earlier open-world game: Shenmue.
Yu Suzuki’s Dreamcast tale of a martial artist seeking revenge for the murder of his father in 1980s Japan immersed the player in an unparalleled level of world-building for the time — dressing its environments in impressive detail, while also encouraging you to simply exist in its world. Its influence can be seen in many an open-world game, including GTA, but perhaps most prominently in the Yakuza series, where minigames, colourful characters and eccentric slices of life can be found on every one of its Japanese and, now, Hawaiian street corners.
From web-swinging superheroes and sword-swinging monster hunters to bank heists and shrine raids.
GTA. There are really no other three letters to start with than Rockstar’s industry-changing creation, especially when it comes to city settings. What started as a top-down, level-based car-stealing simulation in 1997 was fun, but limited by the confines of the technology of the time. It would take another four years, and the creation of the PS2 and its DVD storage capabilities, for the series to truly become a phenomenon as it stepped into the 3D era with Grand Theft Auto 3.

Street Fighter, Stranger Than Heaven, buzzy festival movies, and more.
Despite Sony’s double State of Play this week being a little bit of a dud — though did you catch the hard-as-hell new Resident Evil clip at the very beginning? — the trailer-sphere nonetheless kept chugging along as it always does. We got a new look at Street Fighter and a bunch more trailers ahead of Venice and Toronto Film Festivals for movies that are already catching Oscar buzz, a holdover from gamescom, and an indie game that caught my attention at the Tribeca Festival this past summer. These are the trailers worth checking out this week (and here’s what you missed last week ).

I might never not be taken aback by blond Noah Centineo as Ken, but the tone of this movie remains convincingly super fun. Like Eric Andre spittles in the new trailer, “This is STREET FIGHTERRRRR!”

packages.headline: Bungie Confirms Plans to Sublease Parts of Its Enormous Bellevue Headquarters Following Mass Layoffs

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Bungie has responded after announcing plans to sublease 210,984-square feet of its massive headquarters in Bellevue, Washington, saying this move reflects its continued focus on a “digital first” model.
Bungie Confirms Plans to Sublease Parts of Its Enormous Bellevue Headquarters Following Mass Layoffs
Bungie has confirmed it is "exploring options" to sublease 210,984 square feet of its massive headquarters in Bellevue, Washington, saying the move reflects its continued focus on a "digital first" model.
Following major layoffs across Bungie’s team in June, the studio has made the decision to put a large chunk of its Bellevue headquarters up for sublease, meaning that it’ll be renting out parts of the space to a third party (or parties).
The Game Post broke the news after reportedly reviewing a 10-page advertisement for the building in a commercial leasing brochure, which stated that 210,984 square feet of the building will be available to sublease through September 30, 2035. That’s a long time from now, and one that left fans concerned for Bungie's future projects.
Bungie confirmed the news in a statement sent to The Game Post, stating that this move reflects the company’s growing focus on remote work, which ties into its "digital-first" model.
"Bungie is exploring options to sublease its campus in Bellevue, Washington," a studio spokesperson said. "The studio transitioned to a digital-first model several years ago, and this move reflects the team’s evolving workplace needs and the effectiveness of its remote collaboration. Bungie will continue to maintain a physical office presence in Bellevue."
Responses from the community have been mixed; some argue that this change is only logical, given the massive layoffs that just occurred, while others are about what this could mean for Bungie’s future.
"Bungie is so good at making games (imo) that I wish they could fill all this space and have 2-5 projects at once,” another said . “But with their reduced size now, it’s probably the wise decision."
"This move reflects the team’s evolving workplace needs."
